target_customer: Bands, agents, publicists and venues in the music industry
problem: Booking tours and finding gigs was fragmented; Whitenoise offered a social network with tour mapping and venue and artist search.
product_category: music industry social network and booking tools

technical_complexity.rationale: A directory, mapping and messaging app was standard web engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Value required both bands and venues, a two-sided network, but nothing prevented MySpace or others from adding booking.

market_need_then: No dated evidence of demand was found; MySpace was widely used by bands and venues for promotion in 2007 and booking was a fragmented manual process, but this is not sourced to a dated page.

branding.domain_note: whitenoisenetworks.com returned 503 when fetched; history unknown.

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand found; the name is a common audio term shared by many products.

outcome_analysis: Whitenoise was a two person Winter 2007 YC company building a social network and booking tools for the music industry, and it is now listed inactive. No founder names on the YC page, no funding, no acquisition and no shutdown cause were found, so the cause is not public.
notes: YC page has a Founders heading with no names, so founders is empty. The Dealroom Whitenoise Networks entry describes a mobile security company, a different firm, and is ignored. Competitor search found Venue Czar (xconomy, 2007-10, seen only as a snippet) and MySpace, but those sources are about 7 months after the batch or do not name Whitenoise, so the list is empty. Website returned 503.
